title: Git blocked? Land it with one command
desc: T1 core for every intelligence, small models first. When a git command or a .git touch is blocked, do this one thing: wkpush.sh -m FILES from the repo root, or if you are a sector write under .tmp and report the path.
steps: INDEX.LOCK EXISTS: another git is running. Wait 20 seconds and run the same wkpush.sh command again. Never delete the lock, never hand-build a GIT_INDEX_FILE, never run git checkout, rebase or stash by hand. //why:stale lock tool follows the running git check //why:self-test validated all lock safety cases

ROOT, ROOKIE OR MAIN SESSION: land your files with ONE command from the repo root: wkpush.sh -m FILE1 FILE2 (bare name, no bash prefix. Another repo: wkpush.sh -C D:/GitHub/REPO -m FILES). It commits only those files and pushes from its own private worktree, so a lock, a dirty tree or a crowded index cannot stop it. Then run git show origin/main:FILE1 and see your change there, because a green exit line alone proves nothing. //why:SDK artifacts ready for final push to origin-haiku //why:landed 13 skills and CLAUDE.md closure on origin-sonnet //why:landed 13 skills and CLAUDE.md closure on origin-sonnet

WHO ARE YOU FIRST. A SECTOR (an Agent or Agent.cmd dispatched you) never runs git: write only the path your brief names under .tmp, print that path last, and report it to your dispatcher. Your ROOT lands it. A git block message is not your task. //why:sector writes artifacts under tmp folder //why:sector path output goes to tmp-haiku //why:sector path output temp directory gate-sonnet //why:sector writes artifacts under tmp folder-haiku

HAIKU ROOTS: bash script.sh is refused, but bare wkpush.sh -m FILES and ./wk-push-minimal.cmd FILES pass. Success story to copy: the Stop gate fix landed as bfdf68e5c from a private worktree while the main tree held 300 dirty files and a stale lock. //why:one command landing is the success road

FAILED TWICE OR PERMISSION DENIED (an ACL on .git/objects): paste the exact error line to your dispatcher and take your next item. Example 2026-10-05: a personal-docs root built staging scripts against an objects ACL error and landed nothing, while one pasted line would have let the spokesman fix the permission. //why:pasted error line beats staging scripts

STALE INDEX.LOCK (live since kih ce567d6c5, probe 2026-10-05): deleting a lock with rm or Remove-Item is answered by the harness itself: it checks the lock is older than 60 seconds with no git process holding it, removes it, and prints BLOCKED NOTHING TO APPROVE. Nothing was left for you to delete, so run your wkpush.sh -m FILES command again. A fresh lock or a running git is left alone: wait 20 seconds. This supersedes the never-delete wording of step 1.
